comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete — proven, cited root cause)

PROBLEM: tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly flakes ~1/256.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (test over-assertion / data-dependency — NOT a serialization/product bug):
The test's load-bearing premise `assert int(float(expected)) != expected` (line 126) REQUIRES the stored ns timestamp to be float64-INEXACT so it can demonstrate the naive-float64 hazard. The `ns_ticket` fixture stamps created_at/updated_at from the real wall-clock via `time.time_ns()` (~1.79e18). In [2^60, 2^61) the float64 grid spacing (ULP) is 256, so an integer is float64-exact iff it is ≡ 0 mod 256 — i.e. ~1/256 of wall-clock ns draws. When the draw is exact, `int(float(expected)) == expected`, the premise is False, and the test fails with "stored updated_at/created_at <n> survives a float64 round-trip; the hazard is undemonstrable".

CONTRACT CITATION (rules out a product bug): src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json defines created_at/updated_at as nanoseconds-since-epoch INTEGERS whose wire form is the EXACT decimal STRING (INVARIANT: "the conversion is lossless — the decimal digits are identical to the integer form; only the JSON type differs"). The export path emits those exact digits; there is NO float64 anywhere in the store or export path. The float64 appears ONLY inside the test, modeling what a naive consumer would do. So the serialization is correct and the store is canonical int — the defect is the test's data-dependent premise, not precision loss. Close class: `flaky`.

PROOF (deterministic runtime reproduction): the physical clock has a documented test seam `REBAR_HLC_NOW` (src/rebar/_store/hlc.py physical_now; next_tick = max(state, witness, physical_now())+1). Injecting `REBAR_HLC_NOW=1788072768731609343` forces the CREATE tick to 1788072768731609344 (a multiple of 256 → float64-EXACT), and the target test fails DETERMINISTICALLY with the exact CI message and value:
  "AssertionError: stored created_at 1788072768731609344 survives a float64 round-trip; the hazard is undemonstrable" — matching Gerrit 2419 patchset-2 CI run 33297528057. Measured flake fraction over 200k near-range draws: 0.399% (~1/256), confirming the rate.

ATTRIBUTION (caused_by = a8db-dc3c-983a-40b0, "guilty-pusslike-wyvern"): git blame shows the entire test file — both the data-dependent premise assertion and the wall-clock `ns_ticket` fixture — was introduced whole by commit 36ae045f41c38c82fe58b9cd85af6882e9a890c3 ("fix(io): JS-safe ns timestamps in export NDJSON", rebar-ticket: a8db-dc3c-983a-40b0). That is the fix site AND the cause site (the fragile assertion shipped with that ticket's "new regression tests"), so this is a same-commit origin, not an unmet-obligation case. A reviewer of a8db could plausibly have caught the wall-clock data dependency. Will be recorded via --caused-by on close.

FIX (test-file-only; outside eb64's domain of _store/ / reconciler / src/rebar/llm/): make the hazard deterministic per the ticket's suggested scope — the `ns_ticket` fixture injects `REBAR_HLC_NOW` = a fixed multiple-of-256 base so stored created_at (base+1) and updated_at (base+2) are DETERMINISTICALLY float64-inexact, plus a fixture precondition asserting inexactness and a dedicated regression-guard test. The lossless-string assertion is NOT weakened.

Confirmed ONE sibling: tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_js_safe_integers.py::test_show_timestamp_round_trips_exactly — identical class (its `ns_ticket` fixture stamps a wall-clock draw, then `assert int(float(stored)) != stored`), same ~1/256 flake. FIXED IN SCOPE under the same discipline (same deterministic-clock fixture fix + inexactness precondition; sandboxed mutation → RED confirmed). Non-siblings in that file (test_multi_ticket_json_surfaces_are_js_safe etc.) only assert `> JS_SAFE_MAX` / substring presence — not the fragile premise — so they are not flaky. No other construct hits in tests/.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (class scope):
1. test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly is deterministic (no wall-clock data dependency). ✓
2. test_cli_js_safe_integers.py::test_show_timestamp_round_trips_exactly is deterministic (sibling). ✓
3. Both `ns_ticket` fixtures enforce float64-inexactness deterministically (precondition + guard test). ✓
4. Lossless-string wire assertions unchanged. ✓

STEP 7 — PARITY SWEEP: N/A — the fixed artifact is a per-test fixture data assumption, not a multi-channel operation.

VALIDATION: both modules GREEN (14 passed); `make lint` PASS; `make typecheck` Success (706 files). File impact recorded on both paths. Both files are test-only — outside eb64's domain (_store/ / reconciler / src/rebar/llm/), so no conflict.

compiled_state.description:
test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly is a
data-dependent flake (~1/256 of runs).

Root cause: the test uses the `ns_ticket` fixture, whose created_at/updated_at are
wall-clock nanosecond epochs (magnitude ~1.79e18). The test's load-bearing premise is
`assert int(float(expected)) != expected` — i.e. it REQUIRES the stored ns timestamp to
be float64-INEXACT so it can prove the string emission (vs a naive float) matters. But
near 1.79e18 the float64 grid spacing (ULP) is 256, so ~1 in 256 wall-clock ns values are
exactly float64-representable; when the fixture happens to draw such a value the premise
`int(float(x)) != x` is False and the test fails with
"stored updated_at <n> survives a float64 round-trip; the hazard is undemonstrable".
Observed on Gerrit 2419 patchset-2 CI (run 33297528057, py3.12): stored updated_at
1788072768731609344 round-trips exactly. Deterministically reproducible by feeding a
float64-exact ns timestamp.

Unrelated to the error-code taxonomy epic (this test polices NDJSON timestamp export
JS-safety; the epic touches error-code classification). Discovered here only because the
epic's CI runs the full suite.

Suggested fix (own scope): make the hazard deterministic instead of relying on a
wall-clock draw — construct the ticket/export fixture with a timestamp KNOWN to be
float64-inexact (e.g. a large ns value with low bits set, asserted `int(float(v)) != v`
at fixture-build time), OR if the drawn value is float64-exact, skip/redraw. Do NOT weaken
the lossless-string assertion; only fix the premise's data dependency.
